title: SIMULIA 316-steel shouldered axisymmetric ratcheting specimen
purpose: Exercise the complete geometry-to-result Chaboche route against a public shouldered-specimen experiment while keeping plotted-data uncertainty and numerical convergence independent.
physics: axisymmetric small-strain 316-steel combined-hardening plasticity under asymmetric cyclic end pressure

source.title: Uniaxial ratcheting under tension and compression

execution.evidence: The self-contained mesh reconstructs the public dimensions; the optional official input deck is accepted only when its SHA-256 matches the recorded identity.

observables: Absolute and root-mean-square difference from digitized experimental Figure 4 points.
Independent spatial-mesh and load-path refinement changes.
acceptance: The structure result remains inside the AgentFEM-defined absolute curve-error band after including raster uncertainty.
The final Newton residual is below the declared equilibrium tolerance.
The final two spatial and load-path refinements each change the cycle-peak strain by no more than the declared release tolerance.
limitations: SIMULIA publishes Figure 4 as a raster plot rather than a numerical table; AgentFEM records a conservative digitization uncertainty.
The public Abaqus input uses CAX4R/CAX3 and geometric nonlinearity; AgentFEM uses an independently generated triangular meridian mesh and the current small-strain Chaboche formulation.
Five-cycle development runs have passed curve and equilibrium checks, but 8-to-16 path refinement still changes the fifth-cycle strain by about 3.75%, above the 1% promotion gate.
The full published 100-cycle saturation response remains a release-candidate obligation.
